content.text: {"primary_meaning":"People belonging to God—especially disciples or believers whose spiritual life and fruitfulness depend on union with Christ, the vine.","primary_basis":["John 15:1–6 — Jesus identifies himself as the true vine and his disciples as the branches; abiding in him produces fruit.","John 15:8,16 — fruitful branches are associated with faithful discipleship.","Romans 11:16–24 — natural and grafted branches represent Jewish and Gentile participants in the covenant people, dependent on the sustaining root."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Israel, Jewish people, and Gentiles in relation to the covenant community; branches may be retained, broken off, or grafted in.","basis":["Romans 11:16–24","Jeremiah 11:16–17"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The Messiah or Davidic king as a new shoot or 'Branch' arising from Jesse or David.","basis":["Isaiah 11:1–5","Jeremiah 23:5–6","Jeremiah 33:15–16","Zechariah 3:8","Zechariah 6:12"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Descendants, offspring, or an extending family line.","basis":["Genesis 49:22","Isaiah 11:1","Isaiah 60:21"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Kingdoms, rulers, nations, or their expanding power, represented by branches of a symbolic tree.","basis":["Ezekiel 17:3–10,22–24","Ezekiel 31:3–9","Daniel 4:10–22","Matthew 13:31–32"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Visible growth, works, influence, or fruitfulness flowing from an underlying spiritual source.","basis":["Psalm 1:3","John 15:2–5","Matthew 13:31–32"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Christian teaching most recognizably associates branches with believers abiding in Christ because of John 15. However, the Bible uses branch imagery in several materially different ways, so there is no single context-independent symbolic definition. The singular title 'the Branch' is especially associated with the Messiah and should not automatically determine the meaning of plural 'branches' in other passages."}
